questions.explain: Paul Larsen sailed Vestas Sailrocket 2 at 65.45 knots (about 121 km/h) over 500 m at Walvis Bay, Namibia, in 2012.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through more countries than any other, ten?
questions.explain: The Danube flows about 2,850 km from Germany's Black Forest to the Black Sea through ten countries and four capital cities.

questions.prompt: What is the largest single mass of ice on Earth?
questions.explain: The Antarctic ice sheet holds about 60% of the fresh water on Earth. If it all melted, sea level would rise about 58 m.

questions.prompt: Which glacier in East Antarctica is the largest glacier in the world?
questions.explain: The Lambert Glacier in East Antarctica is about 400 km long and up to 100 km wide.

questions.prompt: What is the largest salt flat in the world, a giant mirror after rain?
questions.explain: Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia covers about 10,600 km² high in the Andes, and holds a huge share of the world's lithium.

questions.prompt: What is the largest river delta in the world, home to the Sundarbans mangroves?
questions.explain: The Ganges–Brahmaputra Delta in Bangladesh and India covers about 105,000 km². The Sundarbans, home to Bengal tigers, grow on it.

questions.prompt: Which geyser in Yellowstone is the tallest active geyser in the world, shooting over 90 m?
questions.explain: Steamboat Geyser in Yellowstone National Park can erupt over 90 m high, but unpredictably, from days to decades apart.

questions.prompt: What is the largest peninsula in the world?
questions.explain: The Arabian Peninsula covers about 3.2 million km² and includes Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman, the UAE, Qatar and Kuwait.

questions.prompt: On which island was Europe's highest temperature, 48.8 °C, recorded in 2021?
questions.explain: A weather station near Syracuse in Sicily recorded 48.8 °C on 11 August 2021, confirmed by the WMO as Europe's record.

questions.prompt: What is the highest temperature recorded in Europe, near Syracuse in Sicily in 2021?
questions.explain: A weather station near Syracuse in Sicily recorded 48.8 °C on 11 August 2021, confirmed by the WMO as Europe's record.

questions.prompt: What is the highest temperature recorded in Europe, near Syracuse in Sicily in 2021, in degrees Celsius?
questions.explain: A weather station near Syracuse in Sicily recorded 48.8 °C on 11 August 2021, confirmed by the WMO as Europe's record.

questions.prompt: Which Argentine research station recorded Antarctica's highest temperature, 18.3 °C, in 2020?
questions.explain: Esperanza Base on the Antarctic Peninsula recorded 18.3 °C on 6 February 2020, the WMO record for the continent.

questions.prompt: What is the highest temperature recorded on the Antarctic continent?
questions.explain: Esperanza Base on the Antarctic Peninsula recorded 18.3 °C on 6 February 2020, the WMO record for the continent.

questions.prompt: What is the highest temperature recorded on the Antarctic continent, in degrees Celsius?
questions.explain: Esperanza Base on the Antarctic Peninsula recorded 18.3 °C on 6 February 2020, the WMO record for the continent.

questions.prompt: Which ski village in New South Wales recorded Australia's lowest temperature, −23 °C, in 1994?
questions.explain: Charlotte Pass in the Snowy Mountains recorded −23.0 °C on 29 June 1994, Australia's official record low.

questions.prompt: What is Australia's highest officially recorded temperature, set at Oodnadatta in 1960 and matched at Onslow in 2022?
questions.explain: Oodnadatta in South Australia recorded 50.7 °C in January 1960, and Onslow in Western Australia matched it in January 2022.

questions.prompt: What is Australia's highest officially recorded temperature, set at Oodnadatta in 1960 and matched at Onslow in 2022, in degrees Celsius?
questions.explain: Oodnadatta in South Australia recorded 50.7 °C in January 1960, and Onslow in Western Australia matched it in January 2022.

questions.prompt: Which Washington ski area measured 1,140 inches (about 29 m) of snow in 1998–99, the most ever measured in one season in the United States?
questions.explain: The Mount Baker Ski Area measured 1,140 inches (95 ft, about 29 m) of snow between July 1998 and June 1999, the US record according to NOAA. The old record, 1,122 inches, was at Paradise on Mount Rainier in 1971–72.

questions.prompt: What is the largest known storm in the Solar System, wider than Earth?
questions.explain: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth that has been raging for at least 190 years, and maybe since the 1600s.

questions.prompt: Which planet is the farthest from the Sun?
questions.explain: Neptune orbits about 4.5 billion km from the Sun and takes about 165 Earth years to go round once. Pluto is no longer counted as a planet.

questions.prompt: Which icy moon of Saturn is the most reflective body in the Solar System?
questions.explain: Saturn's moon Enceladus is covered in fresh ice that reflects almost all the sunlight that hits it. Geysers spray water from its south pole.

questions.prompt: What is the largest space station ever built?
questions.explain: The International Space Station is about the size of a football pitch and has been lived on continuously since November 2000.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which cosmonaut had spent the most total time on spacewalks, about 82 hours?
questions.explain: Anatoly Solovyev made 16 spacewalks, mostly from Mir, totalling about 82 hours, the record as of 2025.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, what was the largest single-dish radio telescope, 500 m across?
questions.explain: China's FAST telescope in Guizhou, finished in 2016, has a 500 m dish built into a natural hollow. It was the largest single dish as of 2025.

questions.prompt: Which flightless parrot from New Zealand is the heaviest parrot in the world?
questions.explain: The kākāpō can weigh up to about 4 kg. It cannot fly, is active at night and is critically endangered.

questions.prompt: Which blue parrot from South America is the longest parrot in the world, about 1 m from head to tail?
questions.explain: The hyacinth macaw is about 1 m long including its tail. Its huge beak can crack coconuts.

questions.prompt: What is the largest kind of penguin?
questions.explain: Emperor penguins stand about 1.1 m tall and weigh up to about 45 kg. They breed in the Antarctic winter.

questions.prompt: Which penguin is the fastest-swimming bird, at about 36 km/h?
questions.explain: Gentoo penguins can swim at about 36 km/h underwater, faster than any other bird.

questions.prompt: Which lemur from Madagascar is the smallest primate, about 30 g?
questions.explain: Madame Berthe's mouse lemur weighs about 30 g and could sit in an egg cup.

questions.prompt: Which bat, also called the bumblebee bat, is the smallest bat?
questions.explain: Kitti's hog-nosed bat from Thailand and Myanmar is about 3 cm long and weighs about 2 g.

questions.prompt: What is the largest wild member of the dog family?
questions.explain: Grey wolves are the largest wild dogs; big males can weigh about 60 kg.

questions.prompt: What is the largest kind of seal?
questions.explain: Male southern elephant seals can weigh up to about 4 tonnes. Their big noses help them roar.

questions.prompt: What is the largest kind of monkey?
questions.explain: Male mandrills of central Africa can weigh about 35 kg. They have bright red and blue faces.

questions.prompt: Which animal has the largest heart, weighing about 180 kg?
questions.explain: A blue whale's heart can weigh about 180 kg, the largest heart of any animal.

questions.prompt: What is the largest known kind of jellyfish?
questions.explain: The lion's mane jellyfish can have a bell over 2 m wide and tentacles over 30 m long.

questions.prompt: What is the largest kind of octopus?
questions.explain: Giant Pacific octopuses can weigh about 50 kg and spread their arms about 6 m across.

questions.prompt: What is the largest kind of shellfish (bivalve)?
questions.explain: Giant clams on coral reefs can be over 1 m across and weigh over 200 kg.

questions.prompt: What is the longest bony fish, up to about 8 m?
questions.explain: The giant oarfish is a ribbon-like deep-sea fish that can be about 8 m long. It may have inspired sea-serpent stories.

questions.prompt: Which fish can make the strongest electric shock of any animal, about 860 volts?
questions.explain: Volta's electric eel from the Amazon can discharge about 860 volts. Despite the name it is a knifefish, not a true eel.

questions.prompt: About how many volts can Volta's electric eel discharge?
questions.explain: Volta's electric eel from the Amazon can discharge about 860 volts. Despite the name it is a knifefish, not a true eel.

questions.prompt: In 2021 scientists found the first animal with over 1,000 legs. What kind of animal is it?
questions.explain: Eumillipes persephone, found deep underground in Western Australia, has up to 1,306 legs, the first millipede with more than 1,000.

questions.prompt: What is the largest bee in the world, about four times the size of a honey bee?
questions.explain: Wallace's giant bee from Indonesia has a wingspan of about 6 cm. It was thought extinct until it was found again in 1981 and photographed in 2019.

questions.prompt: Which living animal has the strongest bite ever measured?
questions.explain: A saltwater crocodile bit down with about 16,000 newtons (3,700 pounds-force) in tests in 2012, the strongest bite measured in a living animal.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which buildings were the tallest twin towers in the world?
questions.explain: The Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur, finished in 1998, are 452 m tall and joined by a sky bridge. They were the tallest twin towers as of 2025.

questions.prompt: What is the largest mosque in the world?
questions.explain: The Masjid al-Haram in Mecca surrounds the Kaaba and can hold over 2 million worshippers during the Hajj.

questions.prompt: What is the longest canal in the world, begun about 2,500 years ago in China?
questions.explain: China's Grand Canal runs about 1,776 km from Beijing to Hangzhou. Its oldest parts are about 2,500 years old.

questions.prompt: Which airport, near Dammam, is the largest airport in the world by land area?
questions.explain: King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia covers about 776 km², bigger than the nearby country of Bahrain.

questions.prompt: Which city has the oldest underground railway in the world, opened in 1863?
questions.explain: The Metropolitan Railway in London opened in 1863 with steam trains. It is now part of the London Underground.

questions.prompt: Where is the tallest lighthouse in the world, about 133 m tall?
questions.explain: The Jeddah Light at the port of Jeddah is about 133 m tall, the tallest lighthouse in the world.

questions.prompt: Who became the youngest person to climb Mount Everest, aged 13, in 2010?
questions.explain: American Jordan Romero reached the top of Everest on 22 May 2010, aged 13. China then set a minimum age of 18 on its side of the mountain.

questions.prompt: Who became the oldest person to climb Mount Everest, aged 80, in 2013?
questions.explain: Japanese skier and climber Yuichiro Miura reached the summit in 2013 at 80. He had skied down part of Everest in 1970.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest muscle in the human body, about 1 mm long and found in the ear?
questions.explain: The stapedius in the middle ear is about 1 mm long. It steadies the stapes, the smallest bone, to protect the ear from loud noise.

questions.prompt: Which film, about 90 minutes long, is the shortest film to win the Oscar for Best Picture?
questions.explain: Marty (1955), about a lonely butcher in the Bronx, runs about 90 minutes, the shortest Best Picture winner.

questions.prompt: Which band is the best-selling music act of all time?
questions.explain: The Beatles have sold an estimated 600 million or more records worldwide, more than any other act.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which act had the most number-one singles on the US Billboard Hot 100?
questions.explain: The Beatles had 20 Billboard Hot 100 number ones, one more than Mariah Carey, the record as of 2025.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which was the most-viewed video on YouTube?
questions.explain: Pinkfong's "Baby Shark Dance" from South Korea passed "Despacito" in 2020 and had over 15 billion views as of 2025.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which YouTube channel had the most subscribers?
questions.explain: Jimmy Donaldson's MrBeast channel passed India's T-Series in 2024 and had the most subscribers as of 2025.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which song had been streamed the most times on Spotify?
questions.explain: The Weeknd's "Blinding Lights" (2019) became the first song to pass 4 billion Spotify streams and was the most streamed as of 2025.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which person had the most followers on Instagram?
questions.explain: Footballer Cristiano Ronaldo had over 600 million Instagram followers as of 2025, more than any other person.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest country in Asia by area?
questions.explain: The Maldives covers only about 300 km² of land, spread over about 1,200 coral islands.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest country in Africa by area?
questions.explain: The Seychelles, an island nation in the Indian Ocean, covers about 457 km², the smallest country in Africa.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest independent country in South America by area?
questions.explain: Suriname covers about 164,000 km², the smallest sovereign country in South America. Dutch is its official language.

questions.prompt: Which Caribbean country is the smallest in the Americas, by area and population?
questions.explain: Saint Kitts and Nevis covers about 261 km² and has about 50,000 people, the smallest country in the Americas.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest country lying entirely within Europe?
questions.explain: Ukraine covers about 604,000 km². Russia is bigger but most of it lies in Asia.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which country had the most people in Africa?
questions.explain: Nigeria had over 220 million people as of 2025, the most in Africa. Lagos is its biggest city.

questions.prompt: Which country has the most lakes in the world?
questions.explain: Canada has more lakes than any other country, by most counts more than half of all the world's lakes.

questions.prompt: Which capital city, on the Caspian Sea about 28 m below sea level, is the lowest national capital in the world?
questions.explain: Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan, lies about 28 m below sea level on the Caspian Sea coast.

questions.prompt: Which Buddhist text, printed in China in 868, is the oldest dated printed book?
questions.explain: A copy of the Diamond Sutra found in a cave near Dunhuang, China, is dated 868. It is now in the British Library.

questions.prompt: Which song carved on an ancient Greek tombstone is the oldest surviving complete musical composition?
questions.explain: The Seikilos epitaph, carved on a stone in what is now Turkey about 2,000 years ago, has both words and musical notes.

questions.prompt: Which zoo in Vienna, founded in 1752, is the oldest zoo still operating?
questions.explain: Tiergarten Schönbrunn in Vienna was founded in 1752 as an imperial menagerie in the palace grounds.

questions.prompt: Which amusement park near Copenhagen, open since 1583, is the oldest operating amusement park in the world?
questions.explain: Dyrehavsbakken, or Bakken, north of Copenhagen, has been entertaining visitors since 1583.

questions.prompt: Which was the world's first national park, created in 1872?
questions.explain: Yellowstone, mostly in Wyoming, became the first national park on 1 March 1872. Australia's Royal National Park followed in 1879.

questions.prompt: Which chili held the Guinness record as the hottest from 2013 until Pepper X beat it in 2023?
questions.explain: The Carolina Reaper, bred by Ed Currie, averaged about 1.64 million Scoville units and held the record from 2013 to 2023.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which country grew the most cocoa beans, the raw material of chocolate?
questions.explain: Ivory Coast grew about 40% of the world's cocoa beans, the most of any country as of 2025.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which country produced the most coffee?
questions.explain: Brazil has been the biggest coffee producer for over 150 years and grew about a third of the world's coffee as of 2025.

questions.prompt: As of 2025, which country produced the most tea?
questions.explain: China grows about half of the world's tea; India is second. It was the record as of 2025.

questions.prompt: Which element makes up the most of the human body by mass?
questions.explain: About 65% of the human body by mass is oxygen, mostly in water. Carbon is second, at about 18%.

questions.prompt: Which metal is the most malleable, so a gram can be beaten into a sheet about a square metre in size?
questions.explain: Gold can be hammered into leaf only a few hundred atoms thick. One gram can cover about a square metre.
